title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, §2.3–2.4. This page explains how the conjectural crystalline de Rham complex DR(f) of 2.2 acquires a Frobenius and becomes a bi-isocrystal. It then explains why integral bi-crystal structures can only be expected for H^1 of abelian schemes.

(1) Frobenius on DR(f). Restrict DR(f) to S_p = V(p) for each prime p. By base change, DR(f)_p = DR(f_p), and DR(f_p)^{(p)} (pullback by the absolute Frobenius of S_p) equals DR(f_p^{(p)}), the cohomology of the relative Frobenius twist X_p^{(p/S_p)} → S_p. The relative Frobenius X_p → X_p^{(p/S_p)} is an S_p-morphism. Contravariant functoriality of DR then gives F_p : DR(f)_p^{(p)} → DR(f)_p. This is the crystalline Frobenius, a σ-semilinear endomorphism of crystalline cohomology.

(2) F is an isogeny. Take the Poincaré-duality pairing DR(f) × DR(f) → T^d[2d], where T^d is the unit crystal with its natural bi-crystal structure (the Tate twist, weight 2d). Transposing F gives a 'Verschiebung' V with FV = VF = a power of p. Hence F becomes invertible after inverting p, and DR(f) ⊗ Q is an F-isocrystal ('bi-isocristal').

(3) Degree-wise statement. Isocrystalline cohomology commutes with arbitrary base change, as R^i f_* of de Rham does in characteristic 0. Hence each DR^i(f) ⊗ Q is itself a bi-isocrystal.

(4) Self-correction of §1.10. He had believed that each integral DR^i(f) is a bi-crystal of weight i (FV = p^i). He now sees this would need a polarization giving an isomorphism, not merely an isogeny, DR^i ≅ DR^{2d-i} ⊗ T^{-(d-i)}. Then V on DR^i would be the transpose of F on DR^{2d-i}, twisted so that V = p^i F^{-1}. Such polarizations exist only exceptionally. In modern terms: p^i F^{-1} need not preserve the lattice H^i_crys. This is related to the Hodge-polygon / divisibility issues later studied by Mazur and Ogus.

(5) §2.4, abelian schemes. Here a genuine integral bi-crystal exists. DR^1(A/S) carries F_p from the relative Frobenius and V_p from the Verschiebung A_p^{(p/S_p)} → A_p (as defined in SGA 3, Gabriel's exposé). On the next page this yields a Dieudonné crystal: the crystalline H^1 of an abelian scheme as its Dieudonné module, i.e. the program later carried out by Mazur–Messing, Berthelot–Breen–Messing and Oda.
errors: Direction/description slip: Grothendieck writes 'le morphisme de frobenius X_p^{(p/S)} → X, qui est un S-morphisme'. The canonical map X^{(p)} → X lies over the Frobenius of S and is not an S-morphism. The S_p-morphism that yields F_p : DR(f_p)^{(p)} → DR(f_p) by contravariance is the relative Frobenius X_p → X_p^{(p/S_p)], i.e. the arrow goes the other way.

'FV = VF = p^{2d}' looks off by a factor of 2. With the Tate crystal T^d having F = V = p^d, transposing F under the pairing gives V = p^d F^{-1}, hence FV = p^d. Possibly this is a convention slip tied to his 'weight 2d' normalization. The isogeny conclusion is unaffected.
Gap: the isogeny claim rests entirely on the postulated duality, which is reasonable for a programmatic letter. The result was later proved (Berthelot's crystalline Poincaré duality).

ideas.what: Crystalline Frobenius on de Rham cohomology via relative Frobenius and base-change compatibility
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Tate, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'), Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); letter to Tate (widely circulated)

ideas.what: F is an isogeny via Poincaré duality, rational cohomology is an F-isocrystal
ideas.modern_name: F-isocrystal structure on H^i_crys ⊗ Q; Verschiebung V = p^d F^{-1} via duality

ideas.what: Integral H^i is not a weight-i bi-crystal in general; this would require a polarization giving an isomorphism with the twisted dual
ideas.modern_name: Failure of p^i F^{-1} to preserve the lattice H^i_crys; Hodge/Newton polygon divisibility (Mazur, Ogus)

ideas.what: H^1_crys of an abelian scheme with F, V from Frobenius and Verschiebung is a Dieudonné crystal
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; Montréal lectures 1970

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known, widely circulated letter to Tate. Its content (crystalline Frobenius, F-isocrystal via duality, the Dieudonné crystal of an abelian scheme) became the foundation of crystalline cohomology and Dieudonné theory, all credited to Grothendieck. The self-correction about integral weight-i bi-crystals is a nice detail, but it anticipates well-documented later work.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the target of f_p^{(p)} is S_p (handwritten p added under S), and the twist is X_p^{(p/S_p)} (with S_p handwritten).
'X_p^{(p/S)} → X' is faithfully transcribed but is mathematically the wrong arrow (see errors).
